items.name: Fogport Tramway System
items.entry:
The Fogport Tramway System is the iron circulation of the city: a common network of narrow-gauge rails carrying passengers, freight, police, fire crews, post, refuse, and the dead. Its principal lines radiate from {{HELIOT}}, while sidings, service loops, and freight branches spread through {{BLACKWAKE}} and the city beyond.

The system grew indispensable after the {{CATASTROPHE}}, when Fogport lost its horses and much of its street plan. Rails were repaired before many roads because a tram can cross mud, broken paving, and districts too cramped for larger steam vehicles. Some lines still pass through arches cut into ruined buildings or make abrupt turns around places the city could not reclaim.

A Common Chassis

Fogport's municipal and commercial trams share a standardized low iron chassis, small flanged rail wheels, compact steam or cable machinery, hand brakes, and common coupling points. Bodies can therefore be built for different duties without redesigning the running gear. Passenger cars, freight flats, fire engines, and police cars all belong visibly to the same mechanical family.

Trams remain subject to the city around them. Rails buckle, points freeze, fog hides stalled cars, and whole routes may close when something nests in a tunnel. Bells warn pedestrians, but experienced Fogporters listen to the rhythm: an ordinary passenger bell, a freight clank, a fire alarm, or the hard double-note that means the civic police are coming.

War and Neutrality

As neutral ground during the {{WAR}}, Fogport receives foreign passengers and cargo from scores of rival powers. The tramway keeps that traffic moving while customs inspectors, embassy agents, smugglers, and refugees crowd the platforms. Neutrality makes the rails international; it does not make them peaceful.

items.name: Standard Passenger Tram
items.entry:
The Standard Passenger Tram is Fogport's ordinary city car: a compact enclosed wooden body mounted on a low iron chassis with small flanged rail wheels. It is a railway vehicle throughout, never a road carriage set upon ordinary wheels.

Cars have open platforms at either end, a conductor's step, brass handrails, roof lamps, destination boards, and windows made from many small panes that can be replaced cheaply after riots, accidents, or monster attacks. Interiors range from varnished and upholstered on prosperous lines to bare slatted benches on working routes. Coal smoke, damp wool, fish baskets, and hot brake iron are its customary atmosphere.

The standard design is deliberately repairable. District workshops exchange wheelsets, brake assemblies, couplers, lamps, and even complete bodies. Individual tram companies paint and decorate their cars differently, but every passenger car remains recognizably part of the same Fogport family.

Passenger trams converge upon {{HELIOT}} and connect the station with markets, docks, civic buildings, factories, respectable neighborhoods, and the edges of poorer districts. Routes are numbered, but locals more often identify them by color, bell-note, conductor, or the particular danger found near the terminus.

items.name: Industrial Freight Tram
items.entry:
The Industrial Freight Tram uses the standard Fogport tram chassis beneath a short locomotive body, open load bed, or skeletal cargo frame. It moves coal, machinery, food, salvage, mail, and standardized {{CRATE_PLURAL}} between the harbor, {{HELIOT}}, the warehouses of {{BLACKWAKE}}, and industrial sidings throughout the city.

Freight cars are squat, heavy, and almost brutally practical. Their beds have iron corner guides and locking dogs positioned to accept the universal crate footprint. A single car may carry one large transit crate or a precisely stacked group of smaller approved loads, depending upon the line and axle rating.

At major depots, overhead cranes lower magnified electromagnets onto the steel lifting plate of each crate. The magnet lands with a hard clink, lifts the load clear, and places it directly into the tram's guides. Dockworkers keep clear until the locking dogs are engaged; dropped crates have flattened more than one careless clerk.

Industrial trams usually travel at night or in gaps between passenger service. Their whistles are lower, their lamps shielded, and their brakes notoriously loud. Smugglers prize them because a sealed universal crate looks much like every other sealed universal crate—until customs asks why its identification marks belong to a country that does not exist.

items.name: Fogport Fire Brigade Tram
items.entry:
The Fogport Fire Brigade Tram is a municipal emergency vehicle built on the standard tram chassis. Its red-painted body carries a steam pump, hose reels, folding ladders, axes, breathing hoods, chemical extinguishers, medical gear, and a compact crew platform guarded by brass rails.

Fire trams are kept under pressure at brigade houses beside major lines. When an alarm arrives, signalmen clear points ahead of them and hold ordinary traffic on sidings. Their rapid hammering bell is legally entitled to the track, though stalled freight, wreckage, crowds, and damaged rails frequently disagree.

A brigade tram cannot reach every burning building directly. It stops at the nearest hydrant spur or cistern point, couples its pump to the municipal water main, and pays out long canvas hoses into the surrounding streets. In districts where water pressure is unreliable, it may tow a tank car or draw directly from a canal.

Fogport fires are rarely simple. Old gas lines, chemical works, coal cellars, crowded timber buildings, and Catastrophe-warped materials can each turn a blaze into something predatory. Brigade crews are respected not because they always save a building, but because they willingly ride toward things from which everyone else is running.

items.name: Civic Police Tram
items.entry:
The Civic Police Tram is the rail vehicle of Fogport's civic constabulary. Built on the standard municipal chassis, it combines a protected driving cab, standing platforms for officers, equipment lockers, powerful lamps, and a barred compartment for prisoners or rescued civilians.

Police trams are used for rapid reinforcement, patrols along tram corridors, prisoner transfers, riot response, and the movement of heavily equipped officers between stations. Their distinctive hard double-bell orders passenger and freight traffic aside. The sound often clears a platform before the tram itself emerges from the fog.

Most carry shields, restraint poles, medical kits, breaching tools, signal rockets, and lockable racks for long arms. Steel shutters can close over the windows when bottles, stones, or worse begin to fly. Some cars tow a plain equipment wagon; others carry evidence lockers lined with lead, salt, or warded timber according to the district.

The tram is formidable but bound to its rails. Barricades, sabotaged points, and ambushes at predictable corners are common countermeasures. Experienced officers therefore dismount before the obvious stop and approach on foot, while inexperienced ones discover that a barred police car can become a prison from either side.

items.name: Standard Transit Crate
items.entry:
The Standard Transit Crate, commonly shortened to transit crate, is the universal freight container used by Fogport and the nations trading through it. The standard does not belong to Fogport alone, and its true place of origin is not presently settled.

Every transit crate has the same approved external dimensions, perfectly square stacking faces, reinforced iron corners fastened by enormous rivets, and a steel lifting plate set into the top. Cranes use magnified electromagnets that descend onto the plate with a characteristic clink, allowing a crate to be lifted, stacked in exact rows, or lowered into the guides of an {{FREIGHT_TRAM}} without slings.

Universal Shape, Foreign Hands

The engineering standard is universal; the crate itself is not. Each culture constructs and decorates its containers according to local materials and habits. Fogport crates tend toward dark timber, black iron, practical stenciling, and repairs made from several earlier crates. Foreign examples may be lacquered, painted, carved, woven over metal frames, clad in patterned sheet, sealed with wax, or decorated with religious and commercial marks.

Despite those differences, every crate carries a white stenciled identification number in the lower-right corner of each marked face. Foreign shippers use their own alphabets and numerical symbols. Dock clerks learn to recognize dozens of scripts, and smugglers invent several more.

Handling and Trade

Transit crates move intact from ship to dock stack, freight tram, warehouse, and outbound vessel. Their standard footprint allows merchants from rival kingdoms to share cranes, rail cars, depots, and storage yards even during the {{WAR}}. In neutral Fogport, that mundane compatibility may be one of the few agreements honored by every belligerent.

Seals and manifests identify the lawful contents. Weight, smell, scratching noises, leakage, and diplomatic flags identify the contents that clerks prefer not to discuss.
